records.title: A case of decompression sickness at 2,437 meters (8,000 feet)
records.author: Rudge FW

observations.outcome_window: Joint pain began suddenly after decompression and persisted through landing. Complete pain relief occurred during recompression. Post-treatment observation duration was not given.
observations.note: Case Report calls the diagnosis presumptive and Discussion questions its specificity. The abstract says there was no diving history, while the case narrative reports a shallow dive ten days earlier. The event date and overlap with broader USAF aggregate treatment archives are unverified.

note: Selected flight with probable bends as judged by the author. The initial clinic diagnosis was patellofemoral pain. No exposure denominator was enumerated.

records.title: Probable bends at 14,000 feet: a case report
records.author: Voge VM

observations.outcome_window: Pain began after about 40 minutes at altitude, persisted two hours after flight and was unchanged on the Monday visit. The author reports essential relief after 20 minutes under the reported conditions and complete relief after one hour of recompression. Formal follow-up duration was not given.
observations.note: Selected flight with probable bends as judged by the author. The initial clinic diagnosis was patellofemoral pain. No exposure denominator was enumerated.

note: The authors describe severe DCS, with subsequent shock and pulmonary edema. No hyperbaric treatment was performed. Clinical and exposure denominators outside this selected report are unavailable.

records.title: A case of decompression sickness in a commercial pilot
records.author: Wolf CW, Petzl DH, Seidl G, Burghuber OC
records.locator: Case Report, abstract and Fig. 2, pp. 990–992

observations.locator: Case Report, abstract and Fig. 2, pp. 990–992
observations.outcome_window: Initial skin symptoms about ten minutes after leveling at flight level 290. Consciousness returned shortly after descent to flight level 100. The abstract reports pulmonary edema and collapse eight hours after landing. The case narrative gives eight hours asleep before symptoms on waking. Hospital discharge was on source day 5.
observations.note: The authors describe severe DCS, with subsequent shock and pulmonary edema. No hyperbaric treatment was performed. Clinical and exposure denominators outside this selected report are unavailable.

note: Second-person teaching vignette with a flight chamber exposure and proposed neurological DCS. Independent patient provenance is not stated.
